faqs.a: Very. Length and weight use internationally defined exact factors — 1 inch is exactly 2.54 cm, 1 pound exactly 0.45359237 kg. Temperature uses the true formulas including the 273.15 Kelvin offset. Displayed results may be rounded, but the underlying math keeps full precision.

This tool follows the computing convention where data doubles in powers of two: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes, 1 MB = 1,024 KB. Storage manufacturers sometimes advertise with 1,000 instead, which is why a “1 TB” drive shows less in your operating system.
Pick the Temperature category, enter your value, and choose Celsius and Fahrenheit in the two dropdowns. The tool applies °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 (and the reverse), so 100 °C becomes exactly 212 °F.
faqs.q: How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?

Extremely large or tiny results switch to scientific notation (like 1.5e+12) because that is how computers display numbers beyond normal range. The value is still exact — it is only the display format that changes.
faqs.q: Why is my result in scientific notation?

unit-converter.formula: For most units: result = value × (from-unit factor ÷ to-unit factor), where each factor is the unit's size in the category's base unit (meter, kilogram, liter, and so on). Temperature is special-cased: °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 and K = °C + 273.15.
howTo: Choose a category such as Length or Temperature.
Type the value you want to convert.
Pick the “from” unit and the “to” unit in the two dropdowns.
Read the instant result plus the conversion-factor line beneath it.
Use Swap to reverse the direction without retyping anything.
keyFacts: Eight categories: length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, time and digital data — 43 units in total.
Length uses exact international definitions: 1 mile = 1,609.344 meters, 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 foot = 0.3048 m.
Temperature uses the real formulas, not approximations — including the 273.15 offset for Kelvin.
Every result shows its conversion-factor line (for example, 1 mile = 1.609344 km) so you can verify the math yourself.
The Swap button flips the from/to units in one tap.
Results are computed live in your browser with full floating-point precision.
limitations: Time conversions use fixed averages (1 year = 365.25 days) — they ignore leap seconds and calendar subtleties.
Data units use the binary computing convention (1 KB = 1,024 bytes); storage makers sometimes use 1,000.
It converts fixed physical units, not currencies or other live rates that change every minute.
Extreme values may display in scientific notation; that is normal floating-point display, not an error.
